react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological process: steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism, FDR 5.74e-15) alongside SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism, rank 1, FDR 5.74e-15) and Reactome R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones, FDR 2.92e-14), all sharing the same five steroid hits. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the sole hit (p = 8.39e-06, 5/87 pathway members matched). Mummichog m/z-direct activity returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the top hit (p = 8.40e-05) with a striking 11/11 network-overlap involving all six androgen/estrogen inputs plus four inferred neighbours; C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism placed second (12/12 overlap). Butan-2-one (KEGG:C02845) and sulindac (KEGG:C01531) were detected only by mass and did not map to the steroid network, explaining their absence from ORA results. Reconcile_InChIKey confirmed all seven input compounds resolve to structurally distinct metabolites (7 unique block-14 clusters, zero conflicts). The biological story is a coordinated dysregulation of the androgen-to-estrogen axis: DHT (C03917), androstenedione (C00280), DHEA (C01227), testosterone (C00535), and 17β-estradiol (C00951) collectively drive enrichment across five databases and two analytical frameworks, implicating altered steroidogenesis as the primary affected pathway.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on the androgen-and-estrogen metabolic axis. RaMP multi-database ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00356 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency at rank 1 with FDR 5.74e-15 and 5 matched steroid inputs out of 27 pathway members. The same five steroids overlapped with SMPDB:SMP00068 Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism at rank 2, and with KEGG:map00150 Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism at rank 3. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-196071 Metabolism of steroid hormones placed sixth with FDR 2.92e-14. WikiPathways WP:WP496 Steroid biosynthesis appeared seventh with 4 matched inputs across 12 members. Mummichog m/z-direct activity returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism with p-value 8.40e-05 and 11/11 network overlap, which includes all five steroid inputs. Mummichog also returned MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism with identical p-value and 12/12 overlap. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 with p-value 4.36e-07, matching the same five steroid inputs across 87 pathway members. Butanone and sulindac did not map to any steroid pathway in any paradigm, consistent with their distinct chemical scaffolds. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies androgen-and-estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism as the primary affected network, driven by five steroid inputs that appear as substrates and products across the mapped reactions.
